title: Ultra-Log-Concavity from a Matrix Recursion
statement: For $n\geq 4$, define $(T_{n+1},Q_{n+1},C_{n+1})^T=M(T_n,Q_n,C_n)^T$, where $M=\begin{pmatrix}z&1+z&1+z\\0&1+z&z\\z+z^2&0&1+z\end{pmatrix}$ and $(T_4,Q_4,C_4)^T=(z^4+2z^3,z^4,2z^4+2z^3)^T$. Writing $V_n=T_n+Q_n+C_n=\sum_kv_{n,k}z^k$, prove that $(v_{n,k})_k$ is ultra-log-concave. More generally, develop criteria for unimodality and ultra-log-concavity of polynomial vectors generated by nonnegative polynomial-matrix recursions.

original_statement: What is a ‘realizable’ M-convex function? What is a ‘Pluecker vector’ of a subspace arrangement? [1] L. PROBLEM 6 (Germain Poullot). Is log-concavity arising through ma- trix recursion? The problem presented here arises when studying the monotone path polytope of the hypersimplex ∆(n, 2). After numerous pages of tedious proofs, one can count the number of coherent monotone paths of ∆(n, 2) thanks to the following matrix recursion. Similar problems give rises to similar question, but we present here a very concrete occurrence, hoping from someone to develop tools to address the general setting.
